why: Round 215 found a 33-case diagnostic file at exactly the path step 3 reads. If runGameTest failed to write, that file would remain and step 3's copy would file it as the run's result - the same shape as the JUnit overwrite, but in the opposite direction: not losing evidence, manufacturing it.
theRiskIsReal: The file is dated 2026-10-07 11:26 and holds 33 cases, while the pending run should produce 129. It sits where the vmArg points, and nothing removes it beforehand.

twoGuardsAddedToStep3.completenessCheckFirst: tools/Test-GameTestCompleteness.ps1 run against the stale file reports expected=129 reported=33 missing=96 and exits 1. Verified by running it, not by reasoning about it.
twoGuardsAddedToStep3.shaFingerprint: The file's SHA-256 begins E743AB3A, recorded in the procedure so an unchanged file is detectable even if a count somehow looked plausible. Verified against the file.
twoGuardsAddedToStep3.theOrderingMatters: The step now says to run the check and see completeness=True before copying anything into docs/evidence, because archiving first and checking later is how a stale file becomes the record.

whyTheCompletenessCheckIsTheStrongerGuar: A fingerprint only proves the file did not change; the check proves it is the right file. Had the stale run happened to contain 129 cases, the fingerprint would still catch it, but the count comparison is what will normally do the work.
